conflicts.fact: Which germination type the bean and maize seeds show (epigeal vs hypogeal), and the associated hypocotyl/epicotyl terms
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 labels bean as epigeal (hypocotyl elongates, cotyledons above soil) and maize as hypogeal (epicotyl elongates, cotyledons stay below). Lesson 1 only describes the observation, so this is consistent. However, Lesson 4 describes the maize seed as having a 'cotyledon' that stays underground as a food reserve, whereas Lesson 8 says the maize 'coleoptile emerges'. Both are compatible, so this is a minor wording difference rather than a conflict.

conflicts.fact: Age and timing of the germination containers, and the stored seed species and storage container in the Kisumu phenomenon
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the transparent containers are at day 3 to 5 of germination. Lesson 4 says the containers are 5 to 7 days old and were prepared since Lesson 3, but Lesson 3 only sets up the experiment on Day 1 using cups. Lesson 2 has the farmer's old seeds as bean seeds stored in a dry gourd, Lesson 3 says bean seeds stored in a dry tin ('dry tin storage from Lesson 2'), and Lesson 2 compares sorghum seeds in its tray.

conflicts.fact: Why the stored seeds failed to germinate (cause)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the stored seeds were dormant, with germination blocked by a hard seed coat or inhibitors, and that dormancy is not death. Lesson 3 says they failed because they had no water, like Cup B in the dry tin. Lesson 6 says abscisic acid held them like a chemical lock even with water and warmth. Lesson 3 contradicts the phenomenon, in which the seeds were given water and warmth.

conflicts.fact: Timing and sequence of the DQB and model references
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says 'Last week we learned' dormancy causes, although the lessons are consecutive, and says the model will be revised in Lessons 4, 5, 6 and 8. Lesson 1 says the model is revised in Lesson 8. Lesson 6 says the model pages were started in Lesson 5, whereas Lesson 1 begins Model Version 1.

conflicts.fact: Role of auxin in etiolation and apical dominance / effect of removing the apical bud
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says etiolation is caused by auxin redistribution and promotes excessive primary growth while suppressing lateral branching, with the remedy of removing the apical bud. Lesson 6 explains that auxin redistribution to the shaded side causes bending (phototropism). Lesson 6 also says bean plants branch more than maize because of apical dominance, which contradicts the claim that maize shows stronger apical dominance than beans while the phenomenon describes beans branching outward.

conflicts.fact: Spindly sukuma wiki and Kisumu phenomenon content
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 phenomenon includes the mango trunk and old seed packet; Lesson 6 introduces a supporting phenomenon of sukuma wiki near a window, and Lesson 8 describes this as part of the Kisumu evidence gallery and adds a new Nakuru farmer problem.
